agent_vs_you: The agent resolved 'the ending' correctly to seconds 5-8 and kept the opening by trimming it, which is right. For the new landing it then planned 'video-edit', a tool the catalogue never offered: catalogue.js filters it out of OFFERED because it is unwired. The model fell back on a generic notion of 'edit a clip'. The catalogue offers a way to build a new ending that joins the old opening exactly. Take the real frame at the cut (frame). Make the landing picture by an image-edit of the original's last frame, with the plane now resting on an open blank notebook. Animate from the cut frame to that end frame (image-to-video with start and end pictures, which the catalogue lists as WELL: 'a move from one picture to another'). Then assemble the untouched opening and the new 3 s clip. The harness made the failure silent. The unwired tool ran as a placeholder SVG and was marked done, and assemble quietly dropped the SVG and delivered 5 s, so a 5-second video came out as 'done'. One more trap the agent avoided only by luck: assemble with seconds 8 and two clips gives each an equal 4 s share, which would cut the opening to 4 s. My plan sets seconds 0 so both clips keep their own length.

fix: Harness: (1) Refuse a plan step whose tool is not in OFFERED before running anything. Re-plan, telling the planner the tool does not exist, instead of writing a placeholder SVG and marking the step done. (2) Make assemble fail when a declared input is missing or not a picture or clip, instead of silently dropping it and delivering a shorter video. (3) Make assemble's seconds allocation give clips their own length and spread only the remainder over pictures (today share = T/n cuts a 5 s clip to 4 s). Do not add an anullsrc track when no piece has sound. Planner rule: 'Change part of a clip = trim the part to keep, frame at the cut, image-edit the new end state, image-to-video from the cut frame to that end frame, then assemble.' Catalogue: 'no tool edits a clip's content in place'.
evidence: The turn-1 paper_plane_animation.mp4 is 858x480, 8.0 s, silent. Frames at 2 fps show a tracking shot following the plane past the window, down to a desk with papers and books, landing there at about 6.5-8 s. In turn 2, notebook_ending.svg is a 923-byte placeholder ('video-edit has no wired endpoint yet'). The final paper_plane_notebook_animation.mp4 is 1280x720 and 5.0 s, with an added silent AAC track. It is only the trimmed opening, upscaled. catalogue.js lists video-edit in TOOLS but excludes it from WIRED and OFFERED. execute.js turns any non-WIRED tool into a placeholder with state 'done'.
